transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, thank you. I came in today because... I just feel like I can't settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like I always have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I'm completely worn out and I really should just be sitting still. It's just exhausting to feel this way.
Have you had this restless, hard-to-sit-still feeling since childhood?

Yes, I have. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always losing my papers, talking out of turn... and they constantly had to give me reminders to just stay in my seat or finish my work. So, yes, it's been there pretty much my whole life.
Have you ever experienced a traumatic event that still affects you now?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've had the usual bumps in the road like anyone else my age, but... no, no major traumatic events or anything like that. Nothing that still bothers me today.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things most days?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I can't get things done or when I lose track of what I'm doing, but... no, I don't sit around worrying about a bunch of different things. My mind is always going a mile a minute, but it's not usually worry.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a lifelong pattern of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity beginning in grade school, with functional difficulties at school (careless work, losing papers, talking out of turn, needing reminders to stay seated and finish work). The patient denies trauma-related symptoms and generalized excessive worry, making PTSD and anxiety disorders less likely. Overall, the presentation is most consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation.
